title: gym_teacher_confiscated_my_shoes
display_title: My gym teacher banned my sneakers over a $0.75 rule I didn't break
beats: My gym teacher confiscated my parkour shoes for the rest of the semester over 75 cents.
Coach Denny had a new rule: any shoe sole thicker than 'regulation' — which he measured himself with a ruler — was banned from the gym.
Mine were three-quarters of an inch over his made-up line, so he zip-tied them together and locked them in his office.
Barefoot parkour finals in four weeks, he said, or I'd fail the unit — forty percent of my grade.
Here's the thing Coach Denny didn't know: those shoes had a tracking chip, because they were also my mom's old work boots, reported stolen property from her job two years ago.
I mentioned that, casually, to the school resource officer during locker inspection week.
Turns out Coach Denny had been 'confiscating' name-brand shoes from kids all year and reselling them online.
He got walked out by the SRO before fourth period, and I got my shoes back the same afternoon — plus an A. Was I wrong to snitch?
